clue.text: It's old, dilapidated, and not easily moved

indicators.note: something dilapidated has fallen apart, so the letters of these words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A crumbling old building that stays put, however hard you push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dilapidated' reshuffles the letters of IT'S OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid person is impassive and unemotional, hard to stir or excite.

clue.text: Tender youth, shy when guarding a prince

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so the throw word surrounds the letters

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to sling

explanation.surface: A bashful young man protects a royal heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' puts A P inside SLING. 'shy' looks like bashful; it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, and figuratively a youth.

clue.text: Old volume, one a lad's binding, shows events

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume

indicators.note: binding means tying round, so these words enclose the numeral

parts.note: a lad is a son, and the 's adds S
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old book, bound by a boy, displays happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' puts I inside A SONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasions are particular events or happenings.

clue.text: Brief independent fellow during convention

indicators.note: during means within, so the abbreviation goes into the word for convention

parts.note: a norm is a convention or standard

explanation.surface: A short independent man appears at a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts F inside NORM. 'Brief' looks like short; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to tell them the facts they need.

clue.text: He agrees to board a ship at the front

indicators.note: says the words 'a ship' come before the verb for boarding

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
to board a vessel is to enter it

explanation.surface: A passenger says yes to going aboard at the bow of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: One who assents is someone giving agreement or consent.

clue.text: Desirable Home Counties axes

parts.note: the counties around London lie in the South East, SE
x and y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Attractive axes for sale in the commuter belt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy is slang for attractive, appealing or fashionable.

clue.text: For one Arab, a self-service display?

definitions.note: an obsession with oneself is cryptically a display of serving the self

parts.note: e.g. means for example, for one
an Omani is an Arab from Oman

explanation.surface: An Arab's way of showing off at a canteen counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-service' is a cafeteria term turned to mean serving one's own ego.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-regard is a display of service to oneself, the question mark marking the wordplay in the definition.

clue.text: Start to turn wrench client picked up on street

indicators.note: picks the opening letter of turn

parts.note: to rick is to wrench or sprain, as in ricking one's neck

explanation.surface: Beginning to twist a wrench, a customer is spotted on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to turn' looks like an instruction; it gives T. A trick is slang for a prostitute's client.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a trick is a punter picked up by a street prostitute.

clue.text: With good reason, furnish hotel at intervals with yen

parts.note: to rig out is to furnish or equip

indicators.note: takes every other letter of hotel

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Kitting out a hotel periodically is justified when yen is on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes H, T, L from HOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something rightly means doing it justly or for sound cause.

clue.text: Placate company head providing wage controls

indicators.note: to control is to hold, so the word for wage holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a wage is pay

indicators.note: the head of the word company is its first letter

parts.note: providing, as a conjunction, means if

explanation.surface: A boss calms the staff by agreeing that wages will be regulated.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate and to pacify both mean to calm or appease someone angry.

clue.text: Revealing former model's status?

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former
a model on the job is posing; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: An ex-model's current situation is laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing something means uncovering it or showing it to view.

clue.text: He deserts the cause, revealing state secrets?

indicators.note: deserts means abandons, so those two letters leave

parts.note: the reason is the cause

explanation.surface: A traitor abandons his cause by leaking official secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' takes HE out of THE REASON. 'He deserts the cause' reads like a defector's description.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country's secrets is a classic act of disloyalty against the state; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: They cover working submariners medical body ignored

indicators.note: working, like a machine in motion, signals that the remaining letters are worked into a new order
ignored means left out, so those letters are dropped from the word submariners

parts.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body

explanation.surface: Submarine crews on duty are left out by the doctors' association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' removes BMA from SUBMARINERS, leaving SURINERS, which 'working' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance companies provide cover against loss or accident.

clue.text: Demand box in opera house

indicators.note: in places the word for box within the opera house's short name

parts.note: the Met is New York's Metropolitan Opera House
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Someone insists on a box seat at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is the Metropolitan Opera in New York; 'box' suggests a theatre box but means a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: There being a market for something means there is demand for it among buyers.

clue.text: Dream team, say, regularly backing supporter

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so the alternate letters follow the supporter

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

indicators.note: takes every other letter of the words team and say

explanation.surface: Dream team, so to speak, steadily backed by a fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, A, S, Y from TEAM SAY; 'backing' puts them after FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasy is a daydream, an imagined scenario.

clue.text: Fine French composer wants one of his own

indicators.note: wants in the sense of lacks, so those letters are missing

parts.note: Charles Gounod wrote the opera Faust
the composer's own word for one, in French, is un

explanation.surface: A French composer is fine but wishes to have one of his own works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks: GOUNOD without UN, French for one, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is fine is saying it is satisfactory or acceptable.

clue.text: Ground-breaking Brown's top skill

definitions.note: the possessive 's here stands for the name Brown is known by

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen
ability is skill

explanation.surface: A pioneering person named Brown shows supreme skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was an 18th-century English landscape gardener who reshaped estates, so he literally broke ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Capability was the nickname of Brown the landscape gardener, whose earthmoving work reshaped English country parks.

clue.text: Inseparable detective leaves unseen

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the detective's letters depart

parts.note: indivisible means unable to be separated
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective walks out without being noticed, though inseparable from his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes DI out of INDIVISIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unseen cannot be perceived by the eye.

clue.text: Return matches make income good for university

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands in for the other

parts.note: revenues are income

explanation.surface: Return fixtures bring in money, good for a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps U for G in REVENUES. 'Return matches' are rematches.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenges, in sport, are return matches played to reverse a defeat.

clue.text: Formally discharge kids, last of 4 lacking uniform

parts.note: issue is a formal word for offspring

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter goes

parts.note: the last of four is the fourth
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A school formally dismisses pupils, the last of four groups having no uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes U from FOURTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue forth is a formal or literary way of saying to come out or emit.

clue.text: What scribe did pointed to missing current account

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters are absent

parts.note: pointed to means indicated

explanation.surface: A finger pointed at a bank statement lacking a current account entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes CA out of INDICATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To indite is an old word for composing in writing, as a scribe would.

clue.text: English minister's retiring at any time

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so these letters are turned round

parts.note: Rev is the abbreviation for a minister, Reverend; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: An English clergyman may be stepping down at any moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever, as in 'if ever', means at any time at all.

clue.text: Free speaker's on holiday

parts.note: re means on, concerning

indicators.note: the speaker's version is how the word for holiday sounds when said

parts.note: leave is time off, a holiday

explanation.surface: An orator announces that he is on holiday and free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaker's' says LEAVE as LIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone is to free them from a burden or duty.

clue.text: Being virtuous, inwardly tense

indicators.note: inwardly means inside, so the word for virtuous takes the letter in

parts.note: moral means virtuous
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Being good makes one nervous inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inwardly' puts T inside MORAL. 'Being' looks like a verb; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a human being, one subject to death.

clue.text: Hamlet, for example, clasping Gertrude at first, runs risk

indicators.note: clasping means holding, so the Dane holds the letter inside

parts.note: Hamlet is the Prince of Denmark, so a Dane

indicators.note: picks the opening letter of Gertrude

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Hamlet embraces his mother Gertrude and runs a risk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clasping' puts G inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger and risk both mean exposure to harm.

clue.text: Midday, end of June, and not a soul

parts.note: midday is noon

indicators.note: picks the final letter of June

explanation.surface: At noon in late June, the streets are deserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a soul means nobody at all.

clue.text: European's mate holds over American championship

parts.note: E is short for European, with the 's adding S

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the friend contains the other letters

parts.note: a mate is a pal
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A European's spouse hosts an American sports title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' suggests a spouse, and 'championship' a sports title; to espouse a cause is to champion it.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousal of a cause is the championing or support of it.

clue.text: Spur teacher to accept first of trainees

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the teacher takes in the letter

parts.note: pupils call a male teacher sir

indicators.note: picks the opening letter of trainees

explanation.surface: A teacher is urged to take on the first of the trainees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts T inside SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone is to rouse or spur them into action.

clue.text: Hard Times tackles hard ideas

indicators.note: to tackle is to grapple with, so the first words take hold of the letter

parts.note: hard means tough
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
T is time, so times is TS

explanation.surface: The Dickens novel Hard Times grapples with difficult ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Hard Times is a Dickens novel, but the words split: 'Times' is TS, T for time twice; H is hard as on pencils.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts are ideas or notions formed in the mind.

clue.text: Firm rejects the Spanish bananas

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so these letters are turned around

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
bananas and bats are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A company turns down a shipment of Spanish bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' turns ELBATS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable and firm both mean steady and not likely to give way.

clue.text: Theatre assistants take notice from speakers

indicators.note: take...from means remove the word for notice
take...from means remove the word for notice

parts.note: addressers are people who address an audience
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Backstage staff take their cues from loudspeakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... from' removes AD from ADDRESSERS. 'speakers' looks like audio equipment; it means people giving addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressers help actors into their costumes in the theatre.

clue.text: Claim drink limits cricket side

indicators.note: limits means bounds, so the drink forms the bounds around the letters

parts.note: ale is beer
leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: Someone asserts that drinking restricts a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side in cricket is the half of the field on the batsman's leg side, not a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim, typically without proof.
